static_traits.name: Zhou Wei
static_traits.occupation: Not yet employed for the time being
static_traits.social_status: Declining social willingness, reduced motivation for meeting new friends; has one friend providing practical support, but unwilling to discuss personal feelings with them
static_traits.medical_history: Has a limb disability (unable to walk), no other significant physical illness; no prior psychological visits/treatment history
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to describe automatic �� thoughts and emotions; neutral attitude with skepticism, but willing to cooperate and explore

basic_info.main_problem: The main problem I want to discuss: I believe my disability will block me from finding a partner, a belief that leaves me lonely and sad.
basic_info.core_demands: I am seeking counseling now because I have noticed that this belief has significantly affected my daily life and overall well-being.
growth_experiences: Three years ago experienced the end of a relationship, which triggered the belief that 'I can't find a partner because of my disability'; since then multiple unsuccessful dating attempts reinforced the belief, and seeing happy couples or thinking about the future intensifies negative emotions (loneliness, sadness).

Long-standing physical disability causing inability to walk; in social and intimate relationship areas, Zhou Wei tends to see the disability as the main barrier, gradually reducing socializing and self-care.

core_beliefs: I am defective, therefore not worthy of love
I am destined not to find a partner

special_situations.event: Seeing happy couples on the street or social media
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others all have partners and I don't, it means my disability dictates that I can never have intimacy
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduced socializing, avoiding meeting new friends to dodge comparison and possible rejection
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I'll never find a partner; I am not as good as them

special_situations.event: Unsuccessful dating attempts (e.g. online dating setbacks)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If one date fails, the reason must be my disability; one failure means every future one will fail too
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Withdrawing quickly after brief attempts, reducing frequency of further dating attempts
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Sure enough, no one would want to be with someone like me

special_situations.event: Thinking about my own future and intimate relationships
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I can't find a partner now, I won't in the future either; loneliness will persist
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reducing investment and self-care to avoid being disappointed again

special_situations.event: Recalling the breakup three years ago
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the relationship breaks up, it means I am essentially unworthy of love, and the disability is the key reason
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids intimacy and emotional investment to avoid being rejected and hurt again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: That breakup proved I have no hope

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be accepted and loved, to build a stable intimate partner relationship
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being rejected because of the disability, being belittled, and persistent loneliness
defense_goal: Lowering the risk of being rejected by avoiding socializing and intimacy
Lowering disappointment through pessimistic anticipation and self-deprecation, gaining pseudo-control

object_relations.self_representation: Defective individual, not worthy of love
object_relations.object_representation: Others/potential partners who may judge or reject oneself

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes reality testing and invites me to look at evidence contrary to the belief
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing the counselor may be negating my real feelings, firmly convinced that 'all evidence supports my view'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Insists 'that is the fact' in the tone of objective evidence; polite but guarded in tone, weakening acceptance of new viewpoints.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor takes friends' support and personal strengths as positive evidence
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing support in friendship has nothing to do with romance, thus keeping emotional distance
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using conceptual distinctions (e.g. 'friendship ≠ romance'), calm tone, creating emotional distance to avoid being touched.

manifestations: Long feeling lonely and sad after the breakup
Pain intensified when seeing happy couples
Believing the disability prevents building intimate relationships
Subjectively experiencing 'being limited, being blocked' due to the physical disability preventing walking
Understands disability as the core obstacle affecting romantic choices and opportunities
outcomes: Avoiding going out and socializing, feeling restricted choices
Forming pessimistic, fatalistic expectations of the future

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: When talking about dating setbacks, presumes potential partners will reject them because of their disability (lacking direct evidence)
Automatically judging myself as unaccepted when seeing couples, internalizing imagined others' evaluations as fact

exception_events.target_problem: In situations of building intimate relationships with others, Zhou Wei typically reduces socializing and withdraws due to thoughts of 'no one will want me', further intensifying loneliness.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In a relationship with a long-supportive friend (e.g. that time the friend bought and gifted a car), he experienced being valued and accepted; the relationship is stable and positive, presenting a connection experience different from the dominant story.
exception_events.reason: Different support: the friend provides sustained emotional and practical support; different understanding: the friend appreciates his being 'good at listening, humorous'; different relationship: a non-romantic relationship lowers evaluation anxiety, making it easier to receive positive feedback.

positive_force: Has a supportive network of friends (friends gave major practical support, e.g. gifting a car)
Having strengths recognized by others (good at listening, humorous)
Willing to seek help and try new methods (seeking counseling, reading therapy books)
Able to reflect in counseling and willing to gradually try reality-testing
negative_force: Deeply rooted negative core beliefs ('I am defective / I am destined not to find a partner')
Cognitive distortions such as catastrophizing, overgeneralization, and mind reading maintaining the problem
Social avoidance and declining self-care, reducing acquisition of positive experiences
Fear of being rejected and shame
Unemployment and living alone reduce daily social contact and outside feedback

antecedent: Thinking about negative expectations of the future
target_behavior.core_reason: Believes 'disability will hinder me from finding a partner', avoids to escape rejection and shame
target_behavior.function: Escaping unwelcome outcomes (being rejected, being compared) and emotional pain
target_behavior.consequence: Fewer opportunities to meet new people, loneliness maintained or worsened

target_behavior.behavior: Self-care and reduced engagement in daily activities
antecedent: Hopelessness after social and dating setbacks
target_behavior.core_reason: Hopeless experiences of believing effort is useless, causing decreased drive
target_behavior.function: In the short term, reduces the pain of facing failure and disappointment
target_behavior.consequence: Daily functioning impaired; low mood maintained or worsening

target_behavior.behavior: Repeatedly engages in negative self-talk (catastrophizing, mind reading, overgeneralization)
target_behavior.core_reason: Negative core beliefs activated, automatic thoughts dominating information processing
target_behavior.function: Gaining pseudo-control through pessimistic expectations, avoiding disappointment after hoping again
target_behavior.consequence: Reinforced hopelessness and inferiority, further weakening social attempts and self-care
